Messages.Author: Scott Halvorson
Messages.Body:
This came up in a game not long ago. A Renegade Garou was in combat
with a vampire. The Garou struck for 2 damage, and the vampire struck
for 4 damage. This damage is enough to kill the Garou. The questions
is this: does the Garou still get his additional strike? I believe he
does, because he doesn't take the damage until the Damage Resolution
step, which comes after all strikes are dealt.

If the vampire had dealt First Strike damage, then the Garou wouldn't
even get his strikes in the first place, would he?

Messages.Author: David Gausebeck
Messages.Body:
>This came up in a game not long ago. A Renegade Garou was in combat
>with a vampire. The Garou struck for 2 damage, and the vampire struck
>for 4 damage. This damage is enough to kill the Garou. The questions
>is this: does the Garou still get his additional strike? I believe he
>does, because he doesn't take the damage until the Damage Resolution
>step, which comes after all strikes are dealt.

Each set of strikes has its own resolution phase. Resolution comes
after all matched strikes are dealt.
So in this case, both guys deal their first strikes and then they
resolve. The garou is dead. So, since there's only one combatant
left, combat is over.

If the garou had lived through the first strike, he would then get to
declare an additional strike.

>If the vampire had dealt First Strike damage, then the Garou wouldn't
>even get his strikes in the first place, would he?

nope. First strike strikes are resolved before normal strikes, and if
you're dead or in torpor when your strike is supposed to resolve,
nothing happens.

It goes something like this:

Both minions declare strike #1 (the one everyone gets)
resolve #1 strikes with first strike
resolve normal #1 strikes
both minions declare strike #2 (first additional strike)
resolve #2 strikes with first strike
resolve normal #2 strikes
both minions declare strike #3 (second additional strike)
resolve #3 strikes with first strike
resolve normal #3 strikes

and so on.

If, after any of these phases, one or both minions are out of the
fight, that's where you stop. Or if both minions are out of
additional strikes.

-Dave

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Troy Montgomery wrote:
> So are you saying if I can do multiple strikes because of celerity I
> can't do multiple strikes if the opposing minion does enough to kill me
> on his first strike?

Yes. In general, you cannot do multiple strikes if the opponent's strike
"kills" you since combat is over when you are "killed", which makes
it impossible to play combat cards (like the ones that would give you
additional strikes). Note: "kill" here consists of burning or going to
Torpor.

VTES Rulebook, section 21. "Advanced Combat Sequence"

1) Establish the range by maneuver. A round of combat can be at close or
long range.
2) Choose your strike. Choose how your minion will strike her opponent:
with a special attack listed on a combat card, a piece of equipment she
possesses, or her bare hands.
3) Check damage.
4) Perform any additional strikes, if possible, and resolve additional
damage.
5) Start another round of combat, if applicable. This is called a press.

"Check Damage" is more appropriately called "Strike Resolution", but
you get the idea.

Later in the same section:

4) Perform additional strikes, if possible: [...]
Additional strikes are announced and performed only
after the initial strikes in the round are completed.

Yes, but this is not usually possible for other reasons (below).

> I.E. Could I play a card that gave me two
> additional strikes then play a card that gave me 1 more additional
> strike for a grand total of 4 strikes?

No, because you can only play one additional-strike-gaining-effect
per round of combat.

The only way to play more is with a card that explicitly
gets around this restriction - like Jacko (Brujah Antitribu)
or Quickness (celerity) - both from the Sabbat expansion.

If you use one of the above-named cards, you can gain
additional strikes, even if the opposing minion did not
get any additional strikes.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <351FF1...@sympatico.ca>, Troy Montgomery
<troy.mo...@sympatico.ca> writes

> AG!!!!! I was taught WRONG!!!!! Ok, here's a question for you then.
>Can I keep playing strike cards that give me multiple strikes even if my

>opponent has none left? I.E. Could I play a card that gave me two

>additional strikes then play a card that gave me 1 more additional
>strike for a grand total of 4 strikes?

No. Only 1 source of additional strikes can be used per round. That
includes things like Vial of Garou Blood or Blur. Jacko and Quickness
violate that rule, but only they do so far, AFAIK.
